# Island supplement sources — V105

This archive accompanies Earth Observer V105. It contains the 23 final geographic RGBA authoring patches, their 23 editable vector extracts, imagery provenance, and license notices. It does not contain the original 8K Earth textures, complete upstream datasets, application binaries, or local development tools.

`manifest.json` is the portable index: every patch has its relative path, SHA-256, WGS84 bounds `[west, south, east, north]`, dimensions, source, adaptations, and corresponding geometry. `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers every other archive file. Coordinates are longitude/latitude degrees, not screen coordinates.

## What is included and how it was adapted

1. **14 legacy global patches:** full-resolution GSHHG L1 coastlines with L2 inland-water holes, version date 2017-06-15; underlying surveys may be older. Only selected missing-land geometry was extracted. Already visible land and a one-original-texel fringe were excluded. Existing source texture colors were sampled where useful; otherwise muted illustrative land color was used. These are not newly acquired satellite observations. Shapes are not artificially enlarged.
2. **3 South China Sea patches:** OSM dry-land and submerged-reef classes remain distinct, with inner lagoon holes. Closed ways, exact-endpoint stitched coastlines, and relation rings supplied the geometry. The rendering excludes `disused=yes`, `abandoned=yes`, and dry-land polygons spanning more than 0.6 degrees longitude. The Nansha extract is the offshore subset: its original geographic filter retained complete features inside 111–117.2 E / 7–12.5 N and excluded features south of 9 N and east of 115.8 E; the final patch has its narrower bounds in the manifest. The supplied GeoJSON retains original tags for auditing, so excluded records must still be filtered when rendering. Regional masks are clipping criteria, not administrative boundaries.
3. **6 modern local replacements:** current OSM coastline extracts dated 2026-11-17 replace legacy GSHHG contours within the Bermuda, Chagos, Maldives, Marshall, Tonga, and Tuamotu detail windows. These are specific windows, not a claim of complete modern coverage of each archipelago. The final 14 legacy PNGs already have their alpha cleared under these windows. `legacy_replacement` in the manifest records the replacement IDs and before/after alpha counts; do not use the earlier untrimmed drafts or double-composite both outlines.
4. **Imagery:** EOX 2025 annual cloud-free mosaics are georeferenced from Web Mercator into WGS84 regional images and clipped to source masks. They are not a single-date or real-time observation. The two direct Copernicus windows are additional Xisha imagery. Source tile URLs and SHA-256 values, acquisition years, CRS and exact coverage are retained in 13 sanitized imagery records. Areas without imagery coverage use illustrative colors on sourced geometry. Water/reef color does not mean dry land or measured depth.
5. **V105 brightness:** the three `scs_*.png` files are the final brighter variants. Encoded sRGB target gain is 1.35 for land and 1.15 for reefs; a shared maximum-channel cap preserves hue without clipping channels to white. Geometry, alpha and geographic bounds are unchanged. Per-patch original/output hashes and measured statistics are in the SCS metadata. This replaces previous patch RGB; it must not be alpha-composited over the old patch a second time.

Historical `preview` or `candidate` labels inside byte-preserved geometry are audit metadata from its preparation, not a prohibition on publication or a statement about the current application version. They do not override the actual upstream licenses. The final source archive index is `manifest.json`.

## Geographic mapping and runtime boundary

For an equirectangular image, `x = (longitude + 180) / 360 * width` and `y = (90 - latitude) / 180 * height`. Regional images run west-to-east and north-to-south. Use the exact bounds and preserve holes and alpha. Legacy longitudes can be unwrapped around the regional window; normalize when mapping across the antimeridian.

These files are editable authoring inputs and source disclosure, not a standalone byte-for-byte build of the complete Earth bundle. The application integration composites color-managed per-mip pixels into affected ASTC blocks of the existing Full base bundle; Shared uses geographic area integration. V105 applies old/new SCS RGB differences to the V104 result while retaining alpha. The original 8K asset reference hash is recorded, but the image and compression tools are intentionally absent from this archive. No shader, nighttime, normal, cloud, or global lighting source is included or changed here.

Tiny islands may remain subpixel at whole-Earth viewing distances. Source geometry and imagery can differ in age or completeness. No fabricated substitute outline was added for a missing source, and this supplement does not claim complete global coverage or survey accuracy.

## Verification

Each final PNG and geometry extract is copied byte-for-byte from the approved authoring inputs. The archive index links each raster to the exact vector and imagery provenance used. Metadata strips local absolute paths; source URLs and upstream tile hashes remain. `SHA256SUMS.txt` enables checking the distributed archive without access to the original workstation. GPL text acquisition and other license source URLs are recorded in `licenses/sources.json`.
